name: Citalopram (Celexa)
qtcDetails: FDA Boxed warning for dose-dependent QTc prolongation (max 40mg/day, max 20mg/day in elderly >60yo or CYP2C19 poor metabolizers). Known risk of TdP.

name: Escitalopram (Lexapro)
qtcDetails: Dose-dependent QTc prolongation (average ~10ms at 20-30mg). Lower risk than racemic citalopram but caution with other QTc agents.

name: Sertraline (Zoloft)
qtcDetails: Minimal effect on QTc at standard therapeutic doses (average ~2-4ms). Preferred SSRI in patients with cardiac comorbidity (SADHART trial).

name: Fluoxetine (Prozac)
qtcDetails: Minimal direct QTc prolongation at typical doses, but potent CYP2D6 inhibition can drastically increase serum levels of other QTc-prolonging drugs.

name: Venlafaxine (Effexor XR)
qtcDetails: Dose-dependent QTc prolongation observed, especially at >150-225mg/day and in overdose. Risk compounded by dose-dependent diastolic hypertension.

name: Duloxetine (Cymbalta)
qtcDetails: Very low intrinsic QTc prolongation risk at clinical doses. Moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor.

name: Bupropion (Wellbutrin)
qtcDetails: Virtually no intrinsic QTc prolongation at therapeutic doses. Primary cardiac concern is tachycardia/hypertension. Potent CYP2D6 inhibitor.

name: Mirtazapine (Remeron)
qtcDetails: Known risk of QTc prolongation, particularly in combination with other QTc agents or in overdose. Sedating at lower doses due to H1 affinity.

name: Trazodone (Desyrel)
qtcDetails: Moderate QTc prolongation risk; cases of ventricular arrhythmias reported when combined with other QTc agents or antiarrhythmics.

name: Quetiapine (Seroquel)
qtcDetails: Moderate, dose-dependent QTc prolongation (~10-15ms). Post-marketing reports of TdP in overdose or when co-administered with CYP3A4 inhibitors.

name: Aripiprazole (Abilify)
qtcDetails: Very low cardiac risk; minimal to no clinically significant QTc prolongation across multiple clinical trials. Often selected when cardiac safety is paramount.

name: Olanzapine (Zyprexa)
qtcDetails: Mild QTc prolongation (~4-6ms). Significantly metabolized by CYP1A2 (cigarette smoking reduces serum levels by ~40-50%).

name: Ziprasidone (Geodon)
qtcDetails: Prominent QTc prolongation (average ~20ms at therapeutic doses). Contraindicated with other drugs that prolong QTc or in patients with known arrhythmias/recent MI.

name: Haloperidol (Haldol)
qtcDetails: High risk of QTc prolongation and Torsades de Pointes, especially with IV administration or high oral doses (>10mg/day). Baseline and interval EKG mandated.

name: Lithium Carbonate
qtcDetails: Causes T-wave flattening/inversion and can cause sinus node dysfunction, sinoatrial block, and secondary QTc prolongation especially at toxic levels (>1.2 mEq/L).

name: Lamotrigine (Lamictal)
qtcDetails: No significant QTc prolongation. Has Class IB antiarrhythmic properties at high doses; FDA safety communication regarding structural heart disease.

name: Ondansetron (Zofran)
qtcDetails: Dose-dependent QTc prolongation. High risk of severe additive prolongation and TdP when co-administered with SSRIs, SNRIs, or antipsychotics.

name: Omeprazole (Prilosec)
qtcDetails: Potent CYP2C19 inhibitor! Significantly increases plasma concentrations of citalopram and escitalopram, compounding their QTc risk.

name: Azithromycin (Zithromax / Z-Pak)
qtcDetails: FDA warning for QT prolongation and potentially fatal Torsades de Pointes. Extreme caution when prescribed alongside psychotropic regimens.

name: Ciprofloxacin / Fluoroquinolones
qtcDetails: Direct block of cardiac HERG potassium channels causing marked QTc prolongation. Potent inhibitor of CYP1A2 (triples olanzapine/duloxetine levels).

name: Hydroxyzine (Vistaril / Atarax)
qtcDetails: FDA/EMA safety alerts regarding dose-dependent QTc prolongation and Torsades de Pointes. Max 100mg/day (max 50mg/day in elderly). Use caution with SSRIs.

name: Dextroamphetamine-Amphetamine (Adderall)
qtcDetails: Does not directly prolong cardiac repolarization (QTc), but increases resting heart rate and blood pressure, which can provoke tachyarrhythmias.
